# Image and Colour Profile 1

Profile hash: `611f1fe5288b9b420a1b9d074996665b087acca982a13cced1491039377b1276`

What a pixel IS, what it MEANS, and the exact numbers every conversion between two of them
uses. "Supports colour management" is not a contract: two implementations can satisfy that
sentence and produce visibly different images, which is what this document exists to prevent.
Every value below is frozen. A change to one is a change to the profile version in the same
edit, and the hash above is what makes that a line in a diff.

## Storage formats

Eight-bit RGB is what a display takes; it is not what a coverage mask, a glyph cache, a filter
intermediate, a wide-gamut composite or an HDR target is made of. Channel order is defined by the
format NAME and never by host endianness.

| format | channels | bits | encoding | bytes | alpha modes | for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `A8_UNORM` | A | 8 | unorm | 1 | straight | coverage masks, glyph masks and alpha-only layers |
| `R8_UNORM` | R | 8 | unorm | 1 | opaque | single-channel data images |
| `R8G8_UNORM` | RG | 8:8 | unorm | 2 | opaque | two-channel data images |
| `B8G8R8X8_UNORM` | BGRX | 8:8:8:8 | unorm | 4 | opaque | scanout, and the commonest firmware hand-off |
| `R8G8B8X8_UNORM` | RGBX | 8:8:8:8 | unorm | 4 | opaque | scanout, the `PIXEL_RGB` firmware hand-off |
| `B8G8R8A8_UNORM` | BGRA | 8:8:8:8 | unorm | 4 | opaque, straight, premultiplied | the ordinary composited surface |
| `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` | RGBA | 8:8:8:8 | unorm | 4 | opaque, straight, premultiplied | the same channel order a decoder produces |
| `R10G10B10A2_UNORM` | RGBA | 10:10:10:2 | unorm | 4 | opaque, straight, premultiplied | wide-gamut scanout |
| `R16G16B16A16_UNORM` | RGBA | 16:16:16:16 | unorm | 8 | opaque, straight, premultiplied | sixteen-bit bounded colour |
| `R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` | RGBA | 16:16:16:16 | float | 8 | opaque, straight, premultiplied | THE CANONICAL INTERMEDIATE: every layer, filter intermediate and offscreen composite |
| `R32_UINT` | R | 32 | uint | 4 | opaque | integer data and object-identity images |
| `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` | RGBA | 32:32:32:32 | float | 16 | opaque, straight, premultiplied | full-float host-visible images |

The canonical intermediate is `R16G16B16A16_FLOAT`, premultiplied and LINEAR: every layer, filter
intermediate and offscreen composite. Repeated compositing through eight-bit sRGB bands and loses
precision, and a blur over an eight-bit intermediate is where it shows first.

`straight` on a format with no alpha channel is a TYPE ERROR and not an unsupported case.
Under `opaque` an alpha channel reads and writes its maximum rather than being carried through
unexamined. And an ALPHA-ONLY format admits `straight` alone: premultiplication is a relation
between colour and alpha, and with no colour there is nothing to have been multiplied.

## What an image means

A normal map, a roughness map, a coverage mask and a depth buffer are all just bytes, and running
any of them through an sRGB decode corrupts them silently. A transfer function applies to colour
and to nothing else.

| semantics | a transfer function applies |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | yes |
| `mask` | NO |
| `normal` | NO |
| `data` | NO |
| `depth` | NO |
| `identity` | NO |

## What may be done to an image

Filtering an identity image averages two object ids into a third that names a different object;
dithering a mask adds noise to coverage; a transfer function on anything but colour is the classic
one. Each refusal below is a defect somebody has shipped.

| semantics | operations |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | `sample`, `filter`, `transfer`, `blend`, `convert-primaries`, `premultiply`, `dither` |
| `mask` | `sample`, `filter`, `blend` |
| `normal` | `sample`, `filter` |
| `data` | `sample`, `filter` |
| `depth` | `sample` |
| `identity` | `sample` |

| storage | may be used for |
| --- | --- |
| `Known(PixelFormat)` | any image: sampled, filtered, drawn into, presented |
| `PackedRgbUnorm` | a boot or scanout adapter's destination only: never sampled, never a texture, never a presentable application surface |

## Allocation and padding

| rule | value |
| --- | --- |
| row alignment | 16 bytes |
| padding on export | zero |
| an allocation below the minimum visible bytes | a typed refusal, from checked arithmetic |
| a zero extent | a typed refusal |

Padding is part of the image's BYTES and not part of the image: never read as pixel content, and
written as zero on export, so two exports of one image are the same bytes - which is what makes an
image hashable and a golden comparison meaningful.

## HDR metadata

Without it a PQ image is untone-mappable: PQ is ABSOLUTE, so a display dimmer than the content has
to know what the content's peak actually was, and "assume ten thousand" tone-maps every image as
though it were the brightest ever made.

| transfer | metadata |
| --- | --- |
| PQ | mastering display minimum and maximum luminance in cd/m², plus maximum content light level and maximum frame-average light level; absent metadata is a refusal to tone-map rather than an assumed peak |
| HLG | the nominal peak luminance in cd/m² the relative signal is referred to; its system gamma follows from that peak |
| SDR | none: an SDR signal is relative to diffuse white, which the profile states |

## Transfer functions

### sRGB

NOT a pure power law, and the linear segment is the part that gets dropped. A 2.2 power law is
close enough to look right and wrong enough that two implementations disagree in the darks, which
is where banding lives.

```text
encoded -> linear:  c <= 0.04045      ->  c / 12.92
                    otherwise       ->  ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ^ 2.4
linear -> encoded:  c <= 0.0031308    ->  c * 12.92
                    otherwise       ->  1.055 * c ^ (1 / 2.4) - 0.055
```

### PQ, SMPTE ST 2084

Its constants are twelve-bit FRACTIONS and are written as such: rounding them to decimals loses
the identity that makes two implementations agree at the endpoints, and the endpoints are where a
display's black level and peak white are decided. PQ is ABSOLUTE: an encoded 1.0 is
10000 cd/m².

```text
m1 = 2610 / 16384        = 0.1593017578125
m2 = 2523 / 4096 * 128   = 78.84375
c1 = 3424 / 4096         = 0.8359375
c2 = 2413 / 4096 * 32    = 18.8515625
c3 = 2392 / 4096 * 32    = 18.6875

encoded -> linear:  Y = ((max(N^(1/m2) - c1, 0)) / (c2 - c3 * N^(1/m2))) ^ (1/m1)
linear -> encoded:  N = ((c1 + c2 * Y^m1) / (1 + c3 * Y^m1)) ^ m2
```

### HLG, ITU-R BT.2100

`b` and `c` are derived from `a` - `b = 1 - 4a` and `c = 0.5 - a ln(4a)` - and are written out
anyway, because a reader checking one implementation against another needs the value rather than
the derivation.

```text
a = 0.17883277    b = 0.28466892    c = 0.55991073

linear -> encoded:  E <= 1/12   ->  sqrt(3E)
                    otherwise   ->  a * ln(12E - b) + c
```

## Chromatic adaptation

BRADFORD, named and written down, because "adapts between white points" is satisfied by three
different matrices in common use and they do not agree. Adaptation happens in this cone space and
in no other.

```text
forward:
  [      0.8951,       0.2664,      -0.1614]
  [     -0.7502,       1.7135,       0.0367]
  [      0.0389,      -0.0685,       1.0296]
inverse:
  [   0.9869929,   -0.1470543,    0.1599627]
  [   0.4323053,    0.5183603,    0.0492912]
  [  -0.0085287,    0.0400428,    0.9684867]
```

## Reference white, tone mapping and gamut mapping

Diffuse white is 203 cd/m². A relative 1.0 in an SDR space is that much light, which is
what makes an SDR image and an HDR image composable at all. Inside the pipeline a linear value may
be negative or above one - a wide-gamut colour in a narrower space is negative, and a highlight is
above one - and clamping happens at OUTPUT and nowhere else.

TONE MAPPING is extended Reinhard, on luminance, with white at 4 times diffuse white:

```text
L_out = L * (1 + L / white^2) / (1 + L)
```

applied to LUMINANCE, with the colour scaled by `L_out / L`, and with luminance taken from the
DESTINATION space's own coefficients: a Rec. 2020 colour's luminance is not its sRGB luminance. One
parameter and exact reproducibility were chosen over a filmic curve, which is prettier and is five
constants two implementations will copy from different sources.

GAMUT MAPPING is hue-preserving desaturation toward equal luminance, by bisection, in 16 steps to a tolerance of
0.000244140625. Clipping each channel shifts hue, and it shifts it most on exactly the
saturated colours a wide-gamut image was made for. A fixed step count is what makes two
implementations produce the same pixels rather than "until it converges".

## Dithering

ordered, Bayer 8x8, with the phase anchored to the target's origin. Error diffusion carries state ACROSS
pixels, which makes a tile-parallel renderer's output depend on how it decomposed the image - so it
is not merely vague here, it is incompatible with the architecture. A tile-relative phase makes the
pattern visibly restart at every tile boundary, which is the artefact that looks like a seam.

The offset added to a channel before quantisation is `(matrix[y % 8][x % 8] + 0.5) / 64 - 0.5` of
one quantisation step, with `x` and `y` the TARGET's coordinates.

```text
   0 32  8 40  2 34 10 42
  48 16 56 24 50 18 58 26
  12 44  4 36 14 46  6 38
  60 28 52 20 62 30 54 22
   3 35 11 43  1 33  9 41
  51 19 59 27 49 17 57 25
  15 47  7 39 13 45  5 37
  63 31 55 23 61 29 53 21
```

## Rounding, at every boundary

| boundary | rule |
| --- | --- |
| float to an integer channel | clamp, then round half away from zero |
| NaN to an integer channel | zero |
| infinity to an integer channel | clamp to the channel extreme |
| float into `R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` | round to nearest, ties to even |
| half-float subnormals | preserved |
| NaN into a half | one canonical quiet NaN |
| an `X8` byte and reserved bits | ignored on read, all bits set on write |

## YUV

| layout | planes | order | subsampling | bits | bit placement | pitch |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| NV12 | 2 | Y, then interleaved CbCr | 2x2 | 8 | the whole byte | luma at least the width; chroma at least the width rounded up to an even number, because its two samples are interleaved |
| I420 | 3 | Y, then Cb, then Cr | 2x2 | 8 | the whole byte | luma at least the width; each chroma plane at least half the width rounded up |
| P010 | 2 | Y, then interleaved CbCr | 2x2 | 10 | the HIGH ten bits of a little-endian 16-bit word; the low six are zero on write and ignored on read | luma at least twice the width; chroma at least twice the width rounded up to an even number |

| matrix | Kr | Kb |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| BT.601 | 0.299 | 0.114 |
| BT.709 | 0.2126 | 0.0722 |
| BT.2020 | 0.2627 | 0.0593 |

Limited range at eight bits is luma 16..235 and chroma 16..240; full range is
0..255. At ten bits: luma 64..940, chroma 64..960, full 0..1023. Getting this wrong is
the single commonest cause of washed-out or crushed video.

| rule | value |
| --- | --- |
| chroma siting | left-sited horizontally, centre-sited vertically, as MPEG-2 and every codec in this tree produce |
| reconstruction | bilinear, with the siting above, edge samples replicated |
| ORDER OF OPERATIONS | reconstruct planes, apply the matrix to encoded RGB, then decode the transfer function, then convert primaries, then premultiply |
| odd extents | chroma extent is the ceiling of half the luma extent; the final sample is replicated |
| crop alignment | a crop origin and extent are multiples of the subsampling factor |

Missing or short planes and invalid layouts are typed refusals, and every per-plane size uses
checked arithmetic.

## Guaranteed minima

A profile with no minima promises nothing: "supports large images" is satisfied by an
implementation that refuses at 513 pixels, so an application written against it discovers the real
limit by being refused, in front of a user. These are the numbers an application may assume without
asking.

| minimum | value |
| --- | ---: |
| image extent, either direction | 16384 |
| pitch, in bytes | 262208 |
| planes | 3 |
| gradient colour stops | 256 |

## Conformance tolerances

So that "passes conformance" has a boundary rather than a judgement. An exact comparison is the
wrong test for a transcendental, and a judgement is not a test at all.

| comparison | tolerance | in |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| a transfer function and its inverse | 0.0000152587890625 | a fraction of full range |
| a colour converted between spaces and back | 0.000244140625 | linear light |
| a tone-mapped value | 0.000244140625 | a fraction of full range |
| a YUV image converted to RGB | 1 | CODE VALUES at the source depth |
| the dither | 0 | EXACT: the matrix and the phase are both stated |
| a filtered sample | 0.0009765625 | a fraction of full range |

## Initialisation

The uninitialised case is a DISCLOSURE rather than an aesthetic problem: a presentable image whose
bytes were never written shows whatever the allocator handed over, which in a system with a shared
page pool is somebody else's pixels - and the bug reads as a flicker rather than as a leak, so it is
not reported.

| when | rule |
| --- | --- |
| a newly allocated image | undefined; a reader before a writer is a defect in the reader |
| before a first present | fully written or cleared; presenting an unwritten surface is refused |
| padding | not content; never read, zeroed on export |

## The three byte spans

Three different questions about one image, and not "the size". An implementation that stores one
number answers all three with it and is wrong about two: it either accepts a buffer that cannot hold
the image, or refuses one that is exactly big enough.

First the two ROW quantities the spans are computed from:

| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| minimum row bytes | `width * bytes_per_pixel` |
| pitch | `the layout's own, at least the minimum row` |

And the three spans:

| span | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `minimum_visible_bytes()` | (height - 1) * pitch + minimum_row_bytes |
| `backend_access_span()` | every byte the selected display or DMA backend may touch, including the final row's pitch padding where it reads that |
| `allocation_len()` | the owned allocation's own length, at least the backend access span for a presentable or DMA image |
